Macro tone from the May 2019 FOMC statement is mildly positive (solid activity, strong labor market, patient stance amid muted inflation). The Beige Book references point to a more mixed underlying backdrop across Districts in March–April: consumer spending was uneven for general retailers and auto dealers; manufacturing activity was hampered by trade-related uncertainty; and agricultural conditions were negatively affected by heavy rainfall and flooding. These dynamics align with the April SLOOS showing tighter bank lending standards (notably for C&I and construction/land development) and softer loan demand across several consumer categories. Net takeaway: still slightly positive, but more cautious than the headline FOMC read due to emerging credit headwinds and sector-specific soft spots.
